paragraphs.title: Ahaz's Sins and the Beginning of Defeat

answers: He did that which was right in the sight of the LORD
He did not that which was right in the sight of the LORD
He refused to reign in Jerusalem
easy.explanation: The KJV says Ahaz did not that which was right in the sight of the LORD.
easy.q: How is Ahaz described at the beginning of the chapter?

easy.explanation: Ahaz walked in the ways of the kings of Israel.
The verse says Ahaz made molten images for Baalim.
easy.q: For whom did Ahaz make molten images?

answers: He burnt them in the fire
He hid them in the Temple
medium.explanation: Ahaz burnt his children in the fire.
medium.q: What did Ahaz do to his children in the valley of the son of Hinnom?

answers: Cast or formed from melted metal
medium.explanation: Molten images were images cast from melted metal.
medium.q: What does the word “molten” mean in “molten images”?

answers: In the high places, on the hills, and under every green tree
Only in the house of the LORD
medium.explanation: The KJV lists the high places, the hills, and every green tree.
medium.q: Where did Ahaz offer sacrifices and burn incense?

answers: He adopted practices forbidden to Israel
challenge.explanation: Burning his children followed the abominations of the heathen whom the LORD had cast out.
challenge.q: Why does the passage call Ahaz’s actions the abominations of the heathen?

answers: He centralized worship of the LORD
He deepened and spread false worship
challenge.explanation: Ahaz practiced idolatry through images, sacrifices, and incense in many locations.
challenge.q: What does the movement from images to sacrifices in many places show about Ahaz?

answers: Between Ahaz and David his father
Between Ahaz and the king of Assyria
challenge.explanation: Ahaz did not do right in the sight of the LORD, unlike David his father.
challenge.q: What contrast is emphasized in the first verse?

paragraphs.title: War Against Judah and the Return of the Captives

easy.explanation: The king of Syria and the king of Israel attacked Judah.
The children of Israel carried away two hundred thousand women, sons, and daughters.
easy.q: How many captives did the children of Israel take from Judah?

easy.explanation: The prophet Oded went out before the host.
easy.q: Who went out before the host that came to Samaria?

answers: Because Israel also had sins against the LORD
medium.explanation: Oded reminded them that Israel also had sins against the LORD.
medium.q: Why did Oded demand that the captives be returned?

medium.explanation: “Fierce wrath” refers to intense anger and judgment.
medium.q: What does “fierce wrath” mean in this passage?

answers: They led the captives into battle
They stopped the army and cared for the captives
They sent the captives to Assyria
medium.explanation: The leaders stood against the returning army and cared for the captives.
medium.q: What did the leaders of Ephraim do after hearing Oded?

answers: The LORD delivered Judah because of its sin, but Israel went too far
challenge.explanation: The LORD was wroth with Judah, but Israel’s cruel treatment added to its own guilt.
challenge.q: What cause-and-effect relationship did Oded describe?

answers: They changed from helpless captives into brothers who needed care
They changed from enemies into soldiers
They changed from slaves into rulers
challenge.explanation: The captives were clothed, shod, fed, and carried to their brethren.
challenge.q: What change in treatment of the captives is shown in the passage?

challenge.explanation: They were brought to Jericho, the city of palm trees, to their brethren.
challenge.q: Where were the captives taken after they were helped?

easy.explanation: Ahaz sent to the kings of Assyria to help him.
easy.q: From whom did Ahaz seek help?

answers: The children of Ephraim and Dan
easy.explanation: The Edomites and Philistines attacked Judah.

answers: The low country and the south of Judah
easy.explanation: The Philistines invaded the cities of the low country and the south of Judah.
easy.q: Which regions did the Philistines invade?

medium.explanation: The Edomites smote Judah and carried away captives.
medium.q: What did the Edomites do to Judah?

medium.explanation: To invade means to enter a place as an attacking force.
medium.q: What does “invaded” mean in this passage?

medium.explanation: The KJV says, “and they dwelt there.”
medium.q: What did the Philistines do in the cities they took?

answers: The invasion was limited to one city
They took control of whole areas
They merely passed through the land
challenge.explanation: Taking cities and their villages indicates broad territorial control.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from the Philistines taking cities with their villages?

answers: Ahaz’s request immediately solved the problem
challenge.explanation: Judah continued to be attacked even after Ahaz sought help.
challenge.q: What does the continued invasion after Ahaz sought Assyrian help emphasize?

answers: They were in the low country and the south of Judah
challenge.explanation: The passage places them in Judah’s low country and southern region.
challenge.q: What geographical description is shared by the Philistine cities mentioned?

paragraphs.title: The Failure of the Assyrian Alliance

easy.explanation: The passage says the LORD brought Judah low because of Ahaz.
easy.q: Because of whom did the LORD bring Judah low?

easy.explanation: Tilgath-pilneser came unto Ahaz and distressed him.
easy.q: Who came to Ahaz and distressed him?

answers: A portion from the LORD’s house, the king’s house, and the princes
easy.explanation: Ahaz gave treasure from the Temple, the royal house, and the princes.
easy.q: What did Ahaz give to the king of Assyria?

answers: Ahaz transgressed sore against the LORD
medium.explanation: The passage connects Judah’s humiliation with Ahaz’s transgression against the LORD.
medium.q: According to the passage, why was Judah brought low?

medium.explanation: The phrase means that Ahaz sinned seriously against the LORD.

answers: The king of Assyria did not help Ahaz
medium.explanation: The KJV explicitly says, “but he helped him not.”
medium.q: What was the result of giving treasure to Assyria?

answers: It did not provide the help Ahaz expected
It returned Judah’s captives to Israel
challenge.explanation: Ahaz gave treasure, but the Assyrian king did not strengthen or help him.
challenge.q: What was the central failure of Ahaz’s alliance with Assyria?

answers: Ahaz’s sin is presented as the reason Judah was brought low
challenge.explanation: The text directly says the LORD brought Judah low because of Ahaz.
challenge.q: What relationship does the passage show between Ahaz’s sin and Judah’s political condition?

answers: He sought Assyrian help when his distress increased
He refused to ask Assyria for help
challenge.explanation: Ahaz sent to Assyria for help, yet even after giving treasure he was not helped.
challenge.q: What does the order of events reveal about Ahaz’s dependence on Assyria?

paragraphs.title: Deepening Sin and the Closing of the Temple

answers: He trespassed yet more against the LORD
He returned to worshiping the LORD
easy.explanation: The KJV says that in his distress Ahaz trespassed yet more against the LORD.
easy.q: What did Ahaz do in the time of his distress?

easy.explanation: Ahaz sacrificed unto the gods of Damascus.
Ahaz shut up the doors of the house of the LORD.
easy.q: What did Ahaz do to the doors of the house of the LORD?

answers: He returned them to the Temple
He hid them with his brothers
medium.explanation: The KJV says Ahaz gathered the vessels and cut them in pieces.
medium.q: What did Ahaz do to the vessels of the house of God?

answers: To act faithfully toward the LORD
To sin against and betray the LORD
To ask the LORD for forgiveness
medium.explanation: To trespass against the LORD means to sin against Him and violate His commands.
medium.q: What does it mean to “trespass against the LORD”?

medium.explanation: He made high places to burn incense unto other gods.
medium.q: What did Ahaz make in every several city of Judah?

answers: He interpreted Syria’s success as proof that its gods had helped it
challenge.explanation: Ahaz believed the gods of the kings of Syria had helped them, so he sacrificed to them.
challenge.q: What does Ahaz’s reasoning for worshiping the gods of Damascus reveal?

answers: They were the ruin of him and all Israel
challenge.explanation: The passage says they were the ruin of Ahaz and of all Israel.
challenge.q: How did the gods of Damascus actually affect Ahaz?

answers: Worship was centralized in the Temple
Worship of the LORD was replaced by widespread false worship
challenge.explanation: Ahaz closed the Temple and established places for other gods throughout the land.
challenge.q: What is the symbolic meaning of closing the Temple doors and building high places throughout Judah?

answers: In the book of the kings of Judah and Israel
In the book of the kings of Assyria
easy.explanation: The KJV says they were written in the book of the kings of Judah and Israel.
easy.q: Where were the rest of Ahaz’s acts written?

easy.explanation: Ahaz was buried in the city, even in Jerusalem.
Hezekiah his son reigned in his stead.

medium.explanation: The passage says they brought him not into the sepulchres of the kings.
medium.q: Was Ahaz buried in the sepulchres of the kings of Israel?

medium.explanation: This expression refers to Ahaz’s death.
medium.q: What does “slept with his fathers” mean in this context?

answers: His deeds were recorded for later generations
medium.explanation: The passage says his acts and ways were written in the historical record.
medium.q: What can be learned from the record of Ahaz’s acts in the book of the kings?

answers: His status and conduct were treated with distinction from the other kings
challenge.explanation: Although buried in Jerusalem, Ahaz was excluded from the sepulchres of the kings.
challenge.q: What does Ahaz’s burial in Jerusalem but outside the royal sepulchres suggest?

answers: Ahaz’s reign ended and Hezekiah began to reign after him
challenge.explanation: After Ahaz died, Hezekiah his son reigned in his stead.
challenge.q: What contrast appears between the end of Ahaz and the beginning of Hezekiah’s reign?

answers: He was honored in the royal sepulchres
His deeds were recorded, but he was not buried in the royal sepulchres
challenge.explanation: The chapter records his deeds, notes his burial outside the royal tombs, and names Hezekiah as his successor.
challenge.q: How does the end of the chapter summarize Ahaz’s position?
